artifact: libcrux ML-DSA (Rust, core modules verified with hax/F*), crate libcrux-ml-dsa v0.0.3; scope described in Bhargavan, 'The strengths and limits of formal verification' (Cryspen, 2026-02-12), https://cryspen.com/post/strengths-and-limitations/
property: Runtime safety and functional correctness of verified ML-DSA core modules against their specification.
model: The verified Rust modules, with platform SIMD intrinsics modeled through verification-friendly wrappers; unverified system libraries and fallback paths outside the proof.
trusted_base: Rust compiler and core::arch SIMD intrinsics
hand-written intrinsic wrappers and fallback implementations
assumptions: platform intrinsics (and their fallbacks) behave as modeled
build target features match those tested in CI
deployed: libcrux-ml-dsa v0.0.3 built for aarch64-unknown-linux-musl on Alpine Linux (Ampere Altra), a target without the SHA3 target feature, producing keys/signatures different from the macOS M2 build.
gap: The verified ML-DSA code was not at fault: per the libcrux maintainers the bug was in an unverified fallback for an aarch64 intrinsic, which produced incorrect ML-DSA output on Alpine/musl aarch64 (a target that, per the issue thread, lacks the SHA3 target feature), a platform path the CI did not exercise.
